title: Specified system compact-support functor and reverse refinement map
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a simultaneous system-operation package $o$ [def-sf-integral-system-operations], with its system interpretation [def-sf-integral-system-expression-domain]. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ and a compactification $c=(j_c,p_c)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], define the system compact-support functor $B_c=S_{p_c}\circ J_{j_c}$ (first $J_{j_c}$, then $S_{p_c}$). Given a finite-field datum $D$ and normalized realization data $\mathcal R$ [def-sf-integral-system-realization-data], and a refinement $r:c\to d$ with quasi-compact $j_c,j_d$, define the reverse refinement transformation $B_d\to B_c$ by inserting the inverse proper-image identity unitor before $J_{j_d}$, applying the specified proper/open map $\Gamma$ for the commuting square with top $j_c$, left $1_X$, right $r$, bottom $j_d$, whiskering by $S_{p_d}$, and then applying the proper-image compositor $S_{p_d}\circ S_r\to S_{p_c}$, using $p_d r=p_c$. The identity unitor is the canonical system bridge followed by the intrinsic semilinear proper-image identity unitor. These are actual functor and natural-transformation constructions; no refinement law or invertibility assertion is included.
